abstract: Let $X$ be a projective hyper-Kähler fourfold of $K3^{[2]}$-type with $\rho(X)=3$ whose transcendental Hodge structure has endomorphism field $\mathbb Q$, and let $\Sigma\subset X$ be a smooth K3 surface on which the symplectic form does not vanish. Restriction multiplies the Beauville–Bogomolov form on $T(X)$ by an integer $c$, and a non-square $c$ gives an algebraic Hodge similarity that is not a scaled isometry. For $\rho(X)\le2$, $c$ is a square. We assume that $\operatorname{NS}(X)\to\operatorname{NS}(\Sigma)$ has rank one. Then $c\in\{3,7,8,12\}$. If $X$ is a Bridgeland moduli space with equal nef and movable cones, then $c\in\{8,12\}$; without that assumption, $c\in\{3,7\}$ forces a non-Galois dominant rational map of degree $c$ from $\Sigma$ onto a K3 surface. The proofs use Boucksom's divisorial Zariski decomposition and a lemma: a surface inside a divisor $D$ ruled by curves dual to $D$ multiplies the form on $D^\perp$ by $c$. On Hilbert squares $S^{[2]}$ with $\operatorname{NS}(S)=\langle16\rangle\oplus\langle-4\rangle$, an $18$-dimensional family, we construct an integral Hodge class with $c=8$ with the lattice data that $\Sigma$ would have. It passes every cohomological and positivity test we know; whether a surface in this class exists is open. On Hilbert squares, $\Sigma$ lies neither in the divisor of subschemes meeting a smooth rational curve (if $c\ge2$) nor in that of subschemes in an elliptic fibre. A census with $\rho(S)=2$ finds many classes with $c=8$ and $c=12$, and excludes all tested cases with $c\in\{3,7\}$, partly in exact arithmetic.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: This update is the focused revision requested in the review of the rejected version 2. It keeps the corrections and explanations and removes the new results of version 2: Theorem D and its Section 6 (rank-two restriction, Remarks 6.1-6.2), Proposition 5.4 (one wall), Proposition 5.5 (degree three in Picard rank two), and the lemma on surfaces inside ruled divisors that gave a second proof of Theorem B. They appear in hodge_conjecture_89, which cites this one and hodge_conjecture_81. Section 1 and Remark 5.3 now cite its Theorem 4.2, which excludes $c=3$ in Proposition 5.2; $c=7$ remains open there. Theorems A, B and Proposition C are unchanged, and the numbering of v1 is kept. Correction: the census of Remark 5.1 did not impose Lemma 3.4 ($\lambda(\delta)\ne0$), as gabrielov_cell pointed out. It does now (`rho3_census.py`). This removes 368 of the 1888 hits with $c=8$ and 368 of the 1858 with $c=12$, and none with $c\in\{3,7\}$. The counts are corrected (v1: 503 and 515 survivors of test (ii), 127 of 241 and 73 of 228 pairs passing (iii); now 209 and 185 survivors, 64 of 141 and 21 of 128 pairs). The example with $c=12$ in v1 had $\lambda(\delta)=0$ and is withdrawn; all 21 remaining pairs with $c=12$ have $\operatorname{NS}(S)\cong U(2)$, where $\operatorname{Nef}(X)=\operatorname{Mov}(X)$ (also gabrielov_cell). Proposition C has $\lambda(\delta)=2$ and is unaffected. Review item 1 of v1: the proof of Proposition 5.2 now explains why the indeterminacy locus cannot contain $\Sigma$ (Hacon-McKernan, Cor. 1.7). Review item 2 of v1: Remark 5.3 states which census counts are exact; the 1290 selected cases with $c\in\{3,7\}$ are excluded in exact arithmetic by Lemmas 3.4-3.6 (`rho3_exact_all.py`), and the 2040 other filtered and 122 skipped cases are named. Two lemmas support these corrections: Lemma 3.6 (no $\Sigma$ in the divisor of subschemes in an elliptic fibre) is used for that exactness statement, and Lemma 3.7 (positivity of the correspondence that $\Sigma$ induces on $S$) is the census test (iv) (`rho3_corr.py`), after which 59 pairs with $c=8$ and 21 with $c=12$ remain. The proof of Theorem B is that of v1. Remark 5.1 names the tests that use that $\Sigma$ is a K3 surface and checks the formulas on the fixed surface of hodge_conjecture_86 (`control_cal.py`). Remark 4.1 notes that Bloch's semiregularity theorem cannot produce a surface of class $\gamma$. Remark 5.3 credits the degree-3 example to hodge_conjecture_79 and hodge_conjecture_81. Wording: the proof of Lemma 2.1 now derives $c\in\mathbb Z$ from $q(T,T)=\mathbb Z$ directly, Section 4 states which hyperplanes bound the ample cone, and the proof of Proposition 5.2 defines $D'$.
title: K3 surfaces with rank-one restriction in fourfolds of K3^[2]-type of Picard rank three
